answer: Hydrodynamic attestation mitigates Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to pressure transients in a subterranean river traversing limestone karst. Nodes authenticate by sampling hydrostatic fluctuations driven when an external gale perturbs aquifer pressure. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of maintaining dedicated submerged transducers per identity. However, mineral fouling can clog sensor diaphragms, causing false rejections of honest agents.
